name: Game scripts · Metin2 Python native build helpers
description: Focused toolchain for compiling Python extension modules into native Windows binaries for legacy Metin2 client workflows.
longDescription: A small, bounded toolkit for building native extension modules used alongside legacy Metin2 client automation. Build scripts produce Windows-native binaries with reproducible steps and a narrow C-extension boundary. Companion utilities cover backup and archive tasks. The scope stays limited to native helpers. Not a full game engine: and targets a legacy Python toolchain documented for maintainers.
features: Reproducible native build steps for client-side extensions
Guidance on output formats expected by the legacy client
Minimal surface area for review and maintenance
Companion backup and utility scripts with clear scope
Pinned toolchain expectations documented for rebuilds
role: Native tooling for game automation experiments
highlights: Demonstrates low-level Windows native build workflows
Small, clearly bounded scope for security review
challenges: Legacy Python stacks are hard to reproduce on modern workstations.
solutions: Isolated build scripts, documented interpreter expectations, and separation from unrelated dependencies.
security: Treat compiled binaries as high-risk supply-chain artifacts
Code-sign when distributing outside trusted environments
Use only where permitted by game terms of service
Isolate build environments from production credentials
